NEW PATIENT VISIT

65 y/o retired elementary school teacher transferring primary care to us from a practice she has been with for many years. Wants one office that keeps track of all her specialists. Lives in Florence.

Problems she brings:
- HTN, long-standing. HCTZ 25 qAM + amlodipine 5. Checks BP at the pharmacy occasionally, "usually in the 120s."
- Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 20 qHS, no side effects.
- Rheumatoid arthritis for years, followed by an outside rheumatology group every 6 months. On methotrexate 15 mg weekly (Saturdays), folic acid daily, prednisone 5 mg daily. Hands "good most days." Rheum gets her monitoring labs through her PCP's lab; will continue that here.
- Breast cancer 2016, treated with surgery and nodal staging at an outside cancer center, finished treatment. Sees oncology yearly with a mammogram.

PSH: L breast lumpectomy with sentinel node biopsy 2016.
Meds: as above, reconciled from her bottles.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: mother had breast cancer after menopause and broke a hip in her 70s. Father had colon cancer. Sister has RA.
SH: Quit cigarettes in 2013. 1-2 glasses of wine a week. No other substances. Taught second and third grade for decades, now retired. Drives, manages her own household and medications.
Screening per patient: colonoscopy in 2018 with prior practice, told it was normal and to repeat in 5 yrs given her father. Has not had a bone density test that she can recall.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, edema. No GI complaints. Some morning stiffness in hands <30 min. Weight stable.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP fine on current regimen. Well appearing woman in no distress. HEENT unremarkable, dentition fair. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Breasts deferred to oncology. Hands: no synovitis today. No edema. Skin without rash.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension - controlled. Continue HCTZ and amlodipine. CMP today.
2. Hyperlipidemia - continue atorvastatin; lipid panel.
3. RA on MTX/prednisone - CBC w diff and CMP today, then every ~3 months for rheum. Long-term steroid use noted; bone density will be due, will order at her wellness visit.
4. Hx breast cancer - oncology surveillance continues; get their notes.
5. Health maintenance - Tdap today (last unknown). Hep C and HIV screening once, ordered. Flu shot when available next month. Welcome-to-Medicare/AWV early next year.
6. Records release signed for prior practice.

RTC 3 months or sooner.

ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB: 01/30/1955   Date of visit: 05/10/2021
Reason for referral: osteoporosis

Thank you for referring Ms. Jacobs, a 66-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis on chronic low-dose prednisone, found on DXA in March to have a lumbar spine T-score of -3.0 with a femoral neck T-score of -2.0. She started weekly alendronate two months ago and is taking it correctly without GI upset. She has had no fractures as an adult. Mother fractured a hip in her early 70s.

Medications reviewed, including prednisone 5 mg daily and methotrexate. Calcium/vitamin D twice daily.

Impression: postmenopausal osteoporosis with a glucocorticoid contribution, no fragility fractures.

Recommendations:
1. Continue alendronate 70 mg weekly. Good choice as first-line therapy.
2. Continue calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 twice daily; dietary calcium is fair.
3. Encourage weight-bearing exercise and fall precautions.
4. Repeat DXA in two years; I will see her then with calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, TSH and 25-OH vitamin D beforehand.
5. Keep the prednisone dose as low as rheumatology can manage.

Endocrinology

GASTROENTEROLOGY
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955
Date of service: 12/26/2022
Referring: primary care

History: 67-year-old woman with about six months of intermittent abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea. On bad days she has as many as six bowel movements, with urgency and incomplete evacuation. Stool infectious studies from your office were negative. Past history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and prednisone 5 mg, osteoporosis on alendronate, and breast cancer treated in 2016. No allergies. Former smoker, light alcohol. Father had colon cancer.

Exam: mildly uncomfortable. Abdomen with mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound or guarding. Rectal: no masses; bright red blood on the examining glove.

Labs (12/26): hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, WBC 9,000, platelets 310,000, CRP 24 mg/L, ESR 40 mm/hr.

Colonoscopy (12/26): continuous inflammation beginning at the rectum and extending proximally, with erythema, loss of the normal vascular pattern and multiple superficial ulcers. Biopsies taken. No masses or polyps seen.

Pathology (12/30): active chronic colitis with crypt abscesses and mucosal ulceration, no dysplasia.

Impression: new diagnosis of ulcerative colitis. Hemoglobin 11.2, likely from blood loss and inflammation.

Plan:
1. Mesalamine 800 mg tablets, one three times daily. Prescription sent.
2. She stays on prednisone 5 mg for her RA; no additional steroid for now.
3. GI follow-up in about 3 months, sooner for worsening bleeding.
4. Recheck CBC with her next methotrexate labs.

Gastroenterology

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - regional hospital
Patient: Arlene Jacobs   DOB 01/30/1955   Arrival 02/19/2026 15:20

Chief complaint: sudden shortness of breath and pain with breathing.

HPI: 71-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer and diverticulitis last August, now 10 days after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for colon cancer (discharged on postoperative day 5), on prophylactic enoxaparin. Two hours ago developed sudden shortness of breath and sharp chest pain on deep breaths. No recent travel. No leg swelling or leg pain.

Home meds per outside list: HCTZ, amlodipine, atorvastatin, methotrexate, folic acid, prednisone 5 mg, mesalamine, letrozole, calcium/vitamin D, enoxaparin 40 mg daily; zoledronic acid also on the list. NKDA.
Social: former smoker, quit about 13 years ago; social alcohol.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air. JVP not elevated. Lungs clear to auscultation. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen with healing laparoscopic incisions. Legs without edema, erythema or tenderness.

Data: ABG on room air pH 7.49, PaCO2 32, PaO2 72, HCO3 24. Chest X-ray unremarkable. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST changes. High-sensitivity troponin I 6 ng/L. CT pulmonary angiogram: acute right lower lobe segmental and subsegmental emboli, RV/LV ratio <1.

Assessment: acute pulmonary embolism, postoperative, in a patient with active cancer. Hemodynamically stable, no RV strain.

Plan: enoxaparin increased to treatment dosing in the ED; supplemental oxygen 2 L to keep saturation above 92%. Admit to medicine for observation and transition to oral anticoagulation.

Course: admitted from the ED 10 days after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (stage I colon cancer), on prophylactic enoxaparin at the time. Discharge medications:

- START apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily. Duration at least 6 months; continue while cancer remains active - to be reassessed by primary care/oncology.
- Continue home medications otherwise unchanged.

TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT

Two hospitalizations this month: lap R hemicolectomy 2/9-2/14 for stage I ascending colon adenocarcinoma (pT2N0, 0/19, margins neg, no chemo), then readmitted 2/19-2/21 with acute R lower lobe PE while on prophylactic enoxaparin. Now on apixaban 10 mg BID through 2/26, then 5 mg BID. Enoxaparin stopped.

Today: breathing much better, no chest pain. No bleeding, stools formed, no blood. Eating smaller meals, weight down about 2 kg since surgery. Walking in the house and to the mailbox. Incisions healing.

Med rec: apixaban added; enoxaparin removed. Others unchanged: HCTZ, amlodipine, atorvastatin, MTX 15 weekly, folic acid, prednisone 5, mesalamine 800 TID, letrozole 2.5 daily, Ca/D BID, chlorhexidine rinse, acetaminophen prn. Zoledronic acid remains off (was still on the hospital's list - asked them to correct).

Exam: VS as charted, SpO2 normal at rest. Comfortable. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abd soft, port sites clean and dry. Calves soft, nontender, no edema.

1. Acute PE, provoked by surgery, with active cancer - apixaban 5 mg BID after loading; plan at least 6 months, then reassess with oncology. Bleeding precautions reviewed. PA approved.
2. Stage I colon cancer s/p R hemicolectomy - surgery f/u April; CEA in May.
